objective: Make holyagent setup and doctor default to the scope the HolyAgent Claude Code plugin is installed at when --scope is not given, instead of always user.
scope: Worktree: /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-scope (branch release/0.3.0/feat/installed-scope-default). Work and run every command there.

Today packages/runtime/src/cli/setup.ts:59 and :99 default to "user", and packages/runtime/tests/setup-scope.test.ts:552 asserts that. Claude Code records an install in enabledPlugins of ~/.claude/settings.json (user), .claude/settings.json (project) or .claude/settings.local.json (local), with local over project over user. Resolve the default from where the HolyAgent plugin id is enabled, with that precedence, reusing settingsFile in packages/runtime/src/setup/scope.ts (it resolves the git top-level and refuses symlinks) and the existing settings readers; find the plugin id the repository already uses rather than inventing one. With no entry anywhere, keep user. A file that does not decode is an error naming the file, as elsewhere in setup.
An explicit --scope always wins. Say in setup's and doctor's output which scope was used and, when it was inferred, from which file, so a user is never surprised by where setup wrote.
Update docs/usage.md:131-139, which says this default is planned, to describe the shipped behavior.

notes:
- **Edits outside ownership:** two existing tests in `setup-cli.test.ts` failed because the new output differs. They are updated, not weakened.
  - The second run of `setup` now starts with `~ scope: user (inferred: ...)`.
  - A broken user settings file in the default search now reports `! scope: <file> is not a JSON object`. I added an assertion that `--scope user` still gives `! user settings:`.
- **Output format:** the first line is `~ scope: <scope> (inferred: holyagent@holyagent is enabled in <file>)` for setup. Doctor prints `ok   scope: ...`. Both also print `(from --scope)` or `(default: ... not enabled in any settings file)`. An undecodable file prints `! scope: <file> ...` or `FAIL scope: ...`, exit 1, and nothing else runs.
- **Symlinks:** the search goes through `settingsFile`, so a symlinked project or local `.claude` makes a no-`--scope` run fail, even for a user-scope install. `--scope user` avoids that. A silent skip would be the alternative; your call.
- **What counts as enabled:** only `enabledPlugins["holyagent@holyagent"] === true`. A `false` entry, or one for another plugin, does not count and the search continues. Managed settings are not consulted.
- **Reading order:** files are read local, project, user and the search stops at the first match, so a bad file later in that order is not reported.

It covers local, project, user, local+project+user, project+user, local+user, none (user default), false or other-plugin entries ignored, doctor inferred and doctor default. Verify exit 0.
- An explicit --scope overrides the inferred one, with a test: same describe, "an explicit --scope overrides the inferred one, in setup and in doctor", plus the `--scope user` case in `setup-cli.test.ts`.
